raw_response:
I will stay with the local two-crop system: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am in Quzhou, and this is still the core system here; recent local results from the Quzhou Experimental Station and county demonstration fields show that the winter wheat-summer maize rotation is the dominant pattern and is performing very well when water and fertilizer are tightened up instead of pushed blindly. I would not spread my land across cotton, peanut, or vegetables this year. At 58, I want a system I know thoroughly, that I can mechanize well, and that fits local water constraints and local service support.

I will plant improved winter wheat in autumn and hybrid summer maize right after wheat harvest. I will manage both crops with balanced fertilization instead of the old heavy-nitrogen habit. The local Quzhou work shows good results around balanced NPK with lower nitrogen than traditional farmer practice, and the county’s 2024 “吨半粮” demonstration reported about 14 kg N/mu on wheat and about 13.8 kg N/mu on maize with very strong yields. So I would keep nitrogen near that level, hold phosphorus and potassium at balanced rates, return straw where possible, and use water-fertilizer integration. For wheat, I would irrigate twice because local North China Plain work supports two key irrigations as the efficient pattern; for maize, I would rely mainly on rainfall and give one supplemental irrigation if needed. I would keep pesticide use controlled and timely rather than frequent, using seed treatment plus targeted field sprays. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage because it fits the tight turnover between the two crops and the local mechanized system.
